explanations.explanation: Every value matches an existing club, so a foreign key to clubs was added safely. Bookings for a club cannot point at a club that does not exist.

The Firebase user id became a uuid column named member_id, generated with uuid5 from the Firebase uid, so row-level security can compare it to auth.uid(). Check that the Supabase auth accounts use the same uuid5 mapping, or the comparison will never match.

The field held a mix of Firestore timestamps and ISO strings, and the strings were parsed into a single timestamp type. Any string in an unexpected format would have failed, so confirm the parsed times look right.

Same approach as the member ids: a uuid named owner_id, derived with uuid5 from the Firebase uid, so ownership checks in row-level security work against auth.uid(). The same mapping must be used when creating auth users.
Its keys vary from document to document, so it is stored as jsonb rather than fixed columns. Queries on individual settings will need jsonb operators, and no column constraints apply to it.
Some rates were numbers and one was a numeric string, which was converted. This is safe, but the rate column should be reviewed to confirm the converted value is correct.
Two numeric strings were converted and one non-numeric value was set to NULL. The NULL is a data loss of that one value, so check whether the original text should be kept elsewhere.
The Firebase user id became a uuid named user_id, generated with uuid5, so row-level security can match it to auth.uid(). This depends on the same mapping being used for auth users.
Every value matches an existing club, so a foreign key to clubs was added safely. Leagues cannot reference a missing club.
Every value matches an existing club, so a foreign key to clubs was added safely. Payments cannot reference a missing club.
The Firebase user id became a uuid named member_id, generated with uuid5, so row-level security can compare it to auth.uid(). It relies on the same mapping as the other user columns.
Its keys vary across documents, so it is stored as jsonb. Expect to query it with jsonb operators, and any field you need often should be promoted to a real column later.
At least 90 percent of documents share the keys last4 and type, so those were flattened into regular columns. Documents missing those keys will have NULLs, which is expected.
This was an array of references, so it became a join table, bookings_players. This keeps player lists queryable and enforces relationships with foreign keys.
This was an array of references, so it became a join table, members_favorite_courts. This keeps favorites queryable and enforces that each court exists.

issues: The proof is recorded as null, which establishes that no result was recorded, not necessarily that it was never run. The checklist's 'pass again' also implies an earlier pass that is not established.
Claims that unexpected timestamp formats would fail, that no column constraints apply to clubs.settings, and that missing payment method keys become NULL are not established by the facts.
The report claims the join tables enforce relationships with foreign keys, but the facts establish only that the join tables were created.
The flagged leagues:read rule's time restriction, request.time < timestamp.date(2026, 12, 31), is omitted; it matters when recreating the policy.
